You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the substantial surrounding scene rendered as a chalk drawing rather than merely softened or textured photographic scenery?
node.criteria: Pass if the substantial environment is re-expressed through chalk-drawn forms and shading. Inspect vegetation, hills, sky and ground separately, including substantial foreground structures. Chalk contours, broken or layered strokes, and rubbed shading may qualify; simplified forms and smooth sky passages are allowed. For broad rubbed passages, look for boundaries, layering or pigment variation that constructs the depicted terrain, vegetation, structures or ground planes, rather than relying solely on source-derived tonal fields. Reduced photographic detail, diagonal streaking, grain or smearing alone does not establish drawn construction. Fail if substantial environmental areas remain photographic modeling softened by blur or texture, even when nearby vegetation or the giraffes show convincing chalk treatment. Do not require every area to contain discrete strokes or regard retained composition as evidence of failure. Return unknown only when evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
node.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for the instruction 'Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk.' Inspect the vegetation, distant hills, sky, foreground ground and left-side structure independently of the giraffes. Compare whether environmental forms have been reconstructed in chalk marks or shading, rather than merely losing photographic sharpness.

node_traces.evidence: The vegetation is softened into broad green smears, and the hills and sky are mostly blurred, streaked tonal fields rather than constructed chalk forms or layered shading. The foreground ground is similarly smooth and smeared, with little drawn definition; the left-side structure retains softened photographic-looking contours. Despite a grainy, chalk-like texture and some treatment on the giraffes, the substantial surrounding scene is not re-expressed as a chalk drawing.

Keep uncertainty for genuinely insufficient visual evidence, not merely because the edit is incomplete."}
